reviews.text: [h3]Please note[/h3] that everything written below was around the time when the game was first "released" (if you could even call it a release). This game had hope but looking at each update and seeing things the dev has said in discord, i cannot in good faith suggest this game to anyone anymore. Its been months and the dev has added plenty of "features" yet STILL doesn't have a working settings screen, which is beyond unforgivable. The game was never ready for a release state and should've been demo'd or had closed testing. The greed of releasing a paid soundtrack alongside a game thats still barely functional leaves a gross taste in my mouth. I would not support this game further if you have the choice too. \/ Old Review Below \/ I dont really write big reviews for games but this game itches such a perfect specific niche in my brain and i love it beyond believe so here it is. Let me be clear, this games themes, soundtrack, and [b]ideas[/b] are IMMACULATE. A horror fps dungeon crawler thats ALSO a rougelike, with a sort of edgy, dying webcore theme/environment? Thats BEYOND incredible, the concept is amazing, the CORE mechanics are incredible. Everything about this game is so incredibly unique in an amazing way. The [i]idea[/i] of the game is beyond perfect. The LOOKS of the game are so well fitting for such an masterpiece of an idea. The UI is very interesting and fitting, although it doesnt feel amazing to play with, but its a smaller issue. The best part about this game is the fking masterful idea that in a rougelike, dying isnt the end of your run, but rather you simply move onto the next floor and lose (as far as i experienced) nearly all of your current resources, so while recovery is possible, you have to [i]really[/i] work for it (at least on the canon mode, that was the only mode i tried). Since the run ends on the final floor, f you feel like you can recover before that, then go ahead and continue, else, the runs arent so long that resetting feels tragic. It keeps the unfair part of rougelike rng out when youre looking for a "perfect run", because chances are in this game, you arent getting that, and if you get screwed early, theres plenty of chances to recover, if you get screwed late, why not go gambling and try to secure a harder soul with less spells so you still have a chance on the last floor? I. LOVE. THIS. CONCEPT. Its enhanced by the writing as well. While the actual lore is hard to follow the characters are more graspable and I do like the interactions of others changing depending on who you pick. [h3]However[/h3] The game is released as a "1.0", meaning it is a full release, the "ready" release. There is no early access tag or demo or anything of the sort for the game. But the game is nearly unplayable [u]in its current state[/u]. At least to [i]seriously[/i] play it. To my understanding there is currently only 1 developer on this game, which is fair, I didnt expect anything to really work flawlessly, especially from what seemed to be an earlier release than intended. [h3]Gameplay[/h3] Spells feel unfinished, they're more flashy than impactful, and half the time it feels like since the physics of the game arent really fleshed out, spells and enemies just randomly kill you and you have no idea [u]why[/u]. Which is very problematic in a game that seems very centered on dying alot to learn information on enemies (how they move, what sounds they make, how to identify them, enements they do, elements theyre weak to, etc.) throughout your runs to understand what to do in each situation. Additionally, because of the unfortunate physics and difficult to digest visuals, its hard to be scared or unnerved when you really just have very little clue whats going on. Text is large, so everything looks scaled weird and uncomfortably displays on larger monitors. This is mostly noticable with the conversational text boxes taking up what feels like half the screen. If the text in the game were a bit smaller, it would unironically be easier to read. Another major problem (although this may be more personal) is that the tutorial of the game is split into a text tutorial and a pseudo-gameplay tutorial. First you read a few pages about the game mechanics, then you get a tutorial room to test some of the features you read before the game actually starts. Maybe my brain is fried or something, but text tutorials dont really work out in any game ive tried recently. For a game with a respeciable amount of mechanics and ui elements, theres just too much stuff to read about and be expected to retain without being bothersome before even [b]playing the game[/b]. It feels like the player is just being thrown every mechanic available at once and if you dont get accustomed to it yourself before starting, its your fault for being unprepared. Now maybe this is a design choice, in which case i could see why, since thematically, it would make sense. However, it feels poor, at least to me. Game has a plethora of bugs, but its recently released game. I can't really complain about bugs right now. With the gameplay feeling very unfinished, i feel like there should've been a free demo or a tag for early access. It can be a bit upsetting to spend $15 and realize there really isnt much to play right now. There are games in early access that have more polish with a similar workforce. [b]This game is more of an experience then an game at the moment. You pay to see the concept and ideas and enjoy everything you can see. Theres even a difficulty just for enjoying the experience, but beyond that, theres nothing that feels smooth or enjoyable to play. Its frankly more fun to just see.[/b] [h3]Why someone SHOULD buy this[/h3] This game has absolutely insane potential and the dev seems like they have very good ideas of where to take it, but from a gameplay standpoint it just lacks so much polish [u]AT THE MOMENT[/u]. So realistically you should just buy it to invest in what could be an amazing game and right now just enjoy the themes and whatnot. Also, supporting solo devs >>>. So many incredible projects have come from small studios and solo devs. If the dev works their ass off, this could be one of the best games ever made. Please buy this for a unique experience and as an investment. [h3]Why someone SHOULD NOT buy this (why this review is negative atm)[/h3] Theres very little "game" available. At least thats playable. Even if you like the thematics, the polish alone will upset you. The game is in "1.0" and it doesnt even have a working sound settings window. Everything feels janky right now, mechanical feedback is poor, everything is so sudden that its hard to have time to process anything, and lastly the visual clarity is very poor (not including the thematics that should make it harder regardless, like glitchy effects and whatnot). Theres no demo or tag for early access so most users probably have no clue what theyre getting themselves into in the first place. This just isnt a game I can recomend right now for someone looking for GAMEPLAY alongside the thematics. That being said, I wouldnt choose to refund this a day in my life. I just hope this game goes the best direction it can and i will be playing every update in hopes to see this game grow into something amazing.

Really interesting game. The visuals are enough to make me want to vomit, but in a profound way, a way that makes you still want to come back, even if it isn't the ideal experience. I enjoy the challenge it offers, and I appreciate the fact that it leaves a lot of the thinking and rationalizing to the player. You are taught basic controls, and past that, you have to use your head to truly understand the mechanics to best benefit yourself. I like the characters, and the story between them and how they interact with each other is super interesting. The roguelite aspect is cool - if you die, it isnt the end of your run, but rather you just move to the next layer with no sigils. This may sound like nothing, but it truly is a climb back. Everyone else has pretty much talked about it as well, but the music is amazing too. I really respect this game and the creator for making something that they were (hopefully) passionate about, knowing that it wasn't going to be ideally liked by most people - even in an age where indie games are more in the spotlight than they ever have been. As a creator, this is the kind of feeling I can only hope to invoke. Excellent work.

这是一种非常典型的、融合了多种现代数字艺术风格的视觉设计。 1. 迷幻艺术 (Psychedelic Art) 特征： 高饱和度、对比强烈的色彩（洋红色、蓝色、绿色），扭曲、流动的形态，以及令人眩晕的图案。这种风格旨在模拟致幻剂下的视觉体验，营造一种超现实、脱离常理的感觉。 2. 故障艺术 (Glitch Art) 特征： 故意模拟数字或模拟信号中的错误和故障，如图像破损、数据损坏、色彩通道错位（RGB Shift）、扫描线失真、噪音和静态干扰。这种风格表达了一种数字世界的非完美、破碎和不确定性。 3. 复古数字/科技美学 (Retro Digital / Tech Aesthetic) 特征： 借鉴80年代和90年代早期计算机图形界面（UI）的元素，如像素字体、简单的几何形状、低分辨率位图、粗糙的渐变和有限的调色板。它唤起了对早期数字时代的怀旧之情，同时也带有一种原始的、未经过度修饰的粗糙感。 4. 低保真恐怖 (Lo-Fi Horror) 特征： 不过度依赖逼真的图形，而是利用模糊、颗粒感、低分辨率、有限的视野和令人不安的音画设计来激发玩家的想象力，从而制造心理上的恐惧感。这种风格认为“未知”和“模糊”比清晰可见的怪物更可怕。 5. 蒸汽波与合成波 (Vaporwave & Synthwave) 的影响 高饱和的粉紫-蓝-绿色调、复古的科技感也深受“蒸汽波”和“合成波”美学的影响。这些文化运动同样迷恋80-90年代的科技、流行文化和数字废墟，并将其与迷幻元素结合。 这将是一场视觉冲击力极强、氛围诡异、在破碎数字领域中进行的超自然体验。

I wish I could give this a fair review, but it's EXTREMELY buggy. Changing the settings sometimes makes your movement lock up; you can see some effects and enemies through text boxes, including other text boxes, making them borderline illegible; The character's full bio floods the left side of the screen for some reason, and that's clearly not meant to happen because it's not in any of the screenshots; mouse sensitivity by default is too high... There's probably a perfectly good game here, and it's one I'd really like to play, but it's too buried in jank for me to reach it, so I ultimately can't recommend the game in its current state. I really hope it gets the QA it needs, because it seems rather charming.

I wouldn't call this game good, but it's definitely interesting. However, I've encountered several bugs in only 30 minutes of gameplay. The game is riddled with bugs, enemies stuck and flipping out of control, auto-aim going crazy and aiming in every direction. It's freaking cool to look at, but just starting the game gave me like 6 speedrunning achievements. The game is so visually loaded that it's hard to tell what's what a lot of the time. Still, I'm really trying to give it a go because I've never seen something like this before. Despite the game being broken, I'm giving this a thumb up just for how f*cking crazy this game LOOKS. [h2] Reply to dev [/h2] Hey dev! First of all, congrats on creating something truly visually unique! This game is, visually, one of the coolest ones I've seen in many, many years. Here are a few things that I think could be easily fixable, even if they're in the game as you intended them. I think that changing the following things would make the game probably more accessible/less frustrating: [list] [*] Seeing the floppy disks through walls can be really confusing for nothing. I'd remove that feature. The disks are eeeverywhere in the maps, no need to be able to spot them through walls. [*] Also, I haven't been able to see further than maybe 2-3 feets from me in some layers because it's so dark and that may be as intended, but I think it's really making those layers just close to unplayable. [*] There seems to be auto-aim when shooting spells, when shooting without activating the lock-on, other times not. I'd personally like to have no auto-aim, because it tends to shoot all over the place at moments and I just wanna shoot where I'm aiming at. Maybe adding an option to toggle it on/off would be great! [*] This is more of a true bug, I don't have much advice on this, but a LOT of the enemies are getting stuck in doorways or seem to have been spawned inside of the floor. [/list] And a personal recommendation; this isn't really an issue or anything, but removing the negative review screenshots from the game, because I feel this could influence people to make negative reviews so that they can be featured in the game. Like I even thought myself "oh f*ck so if I make a sh*t review I'm gonna be featured?". Don't let the bad reviews get to you <3

Firstly I want to start by saying I'd give this review a mixed if I could, This game is just beyond beautiful, it is very well artistically crafted. I love the heavy metal graphics, I love the music (actually fire btw), I love the dialogue and the characters. It is unlike anything else I have played on the market currently, though you can see inspiration it doesn't feel like a straight rip-off. If this game were not created by a small team (I'm pretty sure its literally 1 person right) it could be absolutely on par with the well-known indie games. Unfortunately the game is tainted by its bugs, the achievements basically do not work even when it said I got them on the screen I didn't get them, I got spam achievements for things I never did, which to be honest I thought was a part of the edgy joke vibes to the game so I guess you could leave that as is. The soul grabbing just does not work sometimes I have no idea what I am doing wrong, I play the game as directed and it doesn't work, but again I really enjoyed this myself because it is so nonsensical.. But on a wider audience this just does not work. The codex and lore parts of the game are totally in shambles I have no idea what is happening there either. The concept of this "shooter" not sure if I'd call it that is absolutely so amazing, again I really do believe in this game's potential and love it so so dearly but the execution at times is so poor for a paid game One last thing I want to mention that did kind of catch me the wrong way is the feature of the bad reviews on a lot of floors, this is not really a complaint related to gameplay but it did kind of feel like a child throwing a tantrum. I have heard rather mixed comments about the dev and their response to criticism, I hope you do not take mine in such a way and rather as someone who supports your work and really wants to see you succeed and achieve your dream making these games. Despite my small complaints and this being a mixed review I have left it as positive because I love it so much, genuinely I really do and wish the dev the best, I've bought all of their games and all are equally as enjoyable.
